title: What If Mount Rainier Erupted Tomorrow?

scenes.text: What if Mount Rainier erupted tomorrow? The lava isn't what you should fear.
The danger is a lahar: a river of water, mud and rock. In Colombia in 1985, one raced down a valley at 10 to 30 kilometers an hour.
About 150,000 people live on ground swept by Rainier's lahars and floods over the last 6,000 years.
About 5,600 years ago, the Osceola Mudflow poured out of the mountain and reached the Port of Tacoma.
Rainier hasn't erupted big lately. The last was a light ash dusting in 1894, and bigger ones about 1,100 and 2,300 years ago.
So the threat isn't fire. It's a wall of mud, and it has happened here before.

What if Mount Rainier erupted tomorrow?
The main danger is a lahar, a fast river of mud and rock, and about 150,000 people live where past ones have flowed.
